The content address is not automatically a claim of publisher authenticity.

fields.label: Name
fields.value: BitTorrent v2 metadata and Merkle verification

fields.label: Summary
fields.value: Use v2 metadata fields and SHA-256-based Merkle structures to describe files and verify content at block and piece levels.

value.action: Identify v2 metadata using meta version = 2.
Read file tree to determine the directory and file hierarchy.
Read piece length, which must be a power of two in v2.
For each non-empty file, interpret piece root as the Merkle root built from 16 KiB blocks.
Use piece layers to carry per-piece Merkle root data.
Use SHA-256-based piece hashing and v2 infohashing; use the full hash in btmh magnet links.
When speaking to legacy tracker/DHT message structures, account for the described 20-byte truncated hash.

fields.label: Purpose
fields.value: Authenticate messages using a shared secret and a standardized keyed construction.

fields.label: Steps
value: Agree on a secure hash and shared secret key.
Compute the HMAC over the canonical message representation.
Transmit the message and authentication tag.
Receiver recomputes the HMAC and compares tags using an appropriate constant-time comparison.

fields.label: Caveats
value: Do not substitute naive hash(secret || message) constructions for HMAC.
Key management and message canonicalization remain important.
